chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you are in the state of freedom (not in Ihram), and you kill game in the open land between Al-Bareed and the Sanctuary, then upon you is its compensation. So if you blind its eye, or break its horn, or wound it, you give charity.

key_terms.الْحِلِّ: The open land (outside the sacred precincts)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for killing game while not in Ihram within the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between the major expiation (jaza') for killing game in the Haram while in Ihram and the specific compensation for doing so while in a state of freedom (halal). It highlights the juristic principle that if the animal is merely injured rather than killed, the obligation is reduced to charitable giving (sadaqah), reflecting the proportional nature of restitution in Shia fiqh. This ruling underscores the sanctity of the Meccan precincts and the detailed legal mechanisms for preserving their ecological and ritual integrity.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When you were free (not in Ihram), so you kill the hunt during the free mode, what is between Al-Bareyd (a measurement of distance) up to the Al-Harram, so upon you would be its compensation. So if you were to blind its eyes, or break its horn, or you injure it, so give in charity’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If you are not in the state of Ihram and hunt in non-al- Haram (the sacred area) within a distance of one Barid (a certain unit of measurement) to al-Haram (the sacred area) you must pay the penalty. If you damage its eyes or break its horn, or injure it, you must pay charity.”’
